sunk_cost.note: Reusing existing task files is justified by the fact that no code has changed since planning (same commit c2e8ce1, same session). This is a pragmatic choice, not attachment to prior work.

anchoring.note: All three options were evaluated on their merits. The rejection of Option C (collapsing waves) is well-reasoned: T02 genuinely depends on T01 because concurrent writes require batch upsert to be in place first.

scope_creep.note: Scope is tightly bounded to ACT-06/07/08 as established in D-20260818-002. No new items were added. However, see blind_spots regarding Wave 0 hygiene items.

optimism.note: The decision does not make optimistic claims about timelines or complexity. The sequential wave ordering is conservative and correct given the dependency chain.

recency.note: The decision is informed by the retroactive review (D-20260818-001) which examined all three prior features systematically, not just the most recent one.

blind_spots: D-20260818-002 stated that 'Remaining minor debt items (ACT-01-05, 09-10) should ride along as Wave 0 hygiene since they are trivial.' D-20260818-003 describes only 3 tasks in 3 waves (T01-T03 mapping to ACT-06/07/08) with no mention of a Wave 0 for the hygiene items. Either the Architect folded them into T01-T03, or they were silently dropped. This should be verified during TechLead review.

The decision assumes no code drift because the commit hash is the same (c2e8ce1). However, it does not account for uncommitted changes in the working tree. If any earlier steps in this session modified files without committing, the task plans may be stale. Low risk but worth noting.

risks.risk: Wave 0 hygiene items (ACT-01-05, ACT-09-10) may be lost between decisions
risks.mitigation: TechLead should verify during review whether these items were addressed in the task files or need to be tracked separately.

risks.risk: Skipping Architect re-validation means no second pair of eyes on task decomposition before execution
risks.mitigation: The sequential wave structure (T01->T02->T03) provides natural checkpoints. TechLead review after all waves will catch architectural issues before merge.

recommendation: Agree with the decision. Skipping the Architect re-run is justified given zero code drift (same commit, same session). The wave ordering correctly respects the T01->T02 dependency. The only action item is to ensure the Wave 0 hygiene debt (ACT-01-05, ACT-09-10) from D-20260818-002 is not silently lost -- TechLead should verify coverage during review.
